sections.history: Thirupullabhoothangudi is a small village near Swamimalai, a short distance from Kumbakonam, and its temple is one of the 108 Divya Desams, the abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham. It belongs to Chola Nadu, the Kaveri country so densely sown with Vaishnava shrines. Here Vishnu is worshipped as Valvil Ramar — Rama of the strong bow — with the Goddess Potramaraiyal, 'she of the golden lotus'. Thirumangai Alvar sang the shrine in his Periya Thirumozhi, recalling the story that gives the village its name. The temple is believed to have been built by the Medieval Cholas, with additions by later rulers.
sections.architecture: The temple is laid out in the Dravidian manner of the Chola delta, its sanctum crowned by the Shobhana Vimana. Within, Rama lies in the bhujanga sayanam posture, reclining and facing east — a form so unusual that devotees speak of this as the one Perumal temple where Rama is seen at rest rather than standing with his bow. The Goddess has her own shrine; the temple tank, the Jatayu Theertham, is named for the bird-king of the legend, and the punnai is the sacred tree.
sections.legends: The sthala purana follows the Ramayana. After the eagle-king Jatayu fell fighting Ravana to save Sita, Rama and Lakshmana found him dying, and Rama himself performed his funeral rites here, honouring the bird as a father. The village name is linked to the episode — 'pul' is the Tamil word for bird. As Sita was not with him then, tradition says, the Goddess Lakshmi rose from the golden lotus of the temple tank to stand beside Rama for the rites, and so she is worshipped as Potramaraiyal.
sections.festivals: Vaikunta Ekadashi in Margazhi (December–January) and Rama Navami in spring are natural occasions for a visit to this shrine of Rama. Festival days follow the Sri Vaishnava calendar and shift from year to year, so check with the temple before planning a visit.
sections.experience: This is an intimate temple, and the reclining Rama is its revelation: come expecting the archer and find instead a lord at rest. Spend a moment at the Jatayu Theertham, where a story of loyalty unto death is remembered. Thirupullabhoothangudi lies close to the Divya Desam of Thiruaadhanur and to Swamimalai, so the three are easily visited together from Kumbakonam.

visit.timings: Open daily for morning and evening darshan, with a midday closure; festival days are the busiest. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear is removed before entering. Follow posted rules and the guidance of the priests.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow posted rules and the guidance of the priests.
visit.gettingThere: Thirupullabhoothangudi is a village near Swamimalai in Thanjavur district, about 10 km from Kumbakonam by road. Kumbakonam has the nearest railway station; Tiruchirappalli has the nearest airport.
